title: All-hands: Data Retention Pledge draft
body:
Purpose: scratch notes for my 6–8 minute all-hands segment on our updated data-retention & audit-commitments for Private deployments. Draft is intentionally conversational. Use this to iterate with legal + product + comms.

Opening (30–45s)
- Quick context: customers increasingly asking for stricter retention controls and audit guarantees for on-prem/VPC installs. We listened.
- High level promise: Redwood will publish a clear default retention policy for Private (and a guide for customizing retention in customer-managed environments), plus expands audit logging options and a new compliance checklist for enterprise onboarding.

Why this matters (1m)
- Trust: customers pick Private because they need control and auditability. We need to make that explicit and easy.
- Sales/closing friction: current onboarding stalls when folks ask for docs or configs. Fixing this reduces friction and support load.
- Differentiator: many infra vendors leave retention as an "ops-only" problem. We pair product defaults with docs and tooling.

What we're shipping (1m)
- 3 concrete items by end of Q2 (tentative):
  1) Default retention policy doc and OSS-friendly config templates (json/yaml snippets).
  2) Expanded audit log collection options + sample parsers for common SIEMs.
  3) An enterprise-ready onboarding checklist (KMS/HSM guidance, retention toggles, audit verification steps).
- Beta offering: self-check tool (CLI) for customers to validate retention settings in their deployment (alpha with solutions team).

Script bits (for flow)
- "We built Redwood to make inference predictable — and predictable includes predictable controls over your data. Today we’re committing to clearer, usable defaults and better tooling so you can verify what we say is actually happening in your environment."
- Pause for effect: "This is not about locking you into defaults. It’s about removing uncertainty."

Anticipated tough questions + suggested answers (Q/A)
- Q: "Are you changing how hosted (Redwood API) handles retention?"
  A: No change to hosted today. This announcement is focused on Private/VPC and enterprises that self-manage. If we change hosted retention policies that will be a separate comms plan.
- Q: "Will you be forcing a minimum retention window?"
  A: No — defaults are conservative and documented. Customers can opt for shorter/longer windows; we’ll provide guidance and an audit trail.
- Q: "How does this affect compliance (SOC2/ISO)?"
  A: The checklist aligns with our current certifications; legal is drafting language tying the steps to standard evidence artifacts.
- Q: "Who pays for additional audit storage?"
  A: For Private, customers manage their storage. For our Managed Dedicated offers we will surface cost estimates and a recommended retention config.

Open technical notes for eng leads (copy these to PRD)
- retention config will live in deployment config under key: retention.policy.* (placeholder name) — need to standardize key names across packages.
- audit log formats: prefer newline-delimited JSON; include canonical fields: timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, requester_id (masked), token_counts, decision_flags. Need sign-off from privacy/legal on field list.
- CLI self-check: simple check: can you list retention setting? can you sample logs older/newer than retention? verify KMS integration for key rotation.

Operations & rollout plan (high level)
- Week 0: legal + product finalize recommended defaults.
- Week 1–3: eng implements config keys + sample parsers.
- Week 4: solutions builds onboarding checklist + test-run with 2 pilot customers.
- Week 6: documentation patch, blog + support playbook, internal training.

Comms plan (internal/public)
- Internal: all-hands (this talk), follow-up detailed doc in Confluence, training session for solutions eng + support.
- External: blog post + technical deep-dive, customer email to active Private/Dedicated accounts, updated docs in GH/Docs site.

Notes to self / friction points to resolve
- Need explicit language from legal on "audit evidence" vs "retained data" — liaise with Ruth.
- Pricing guidance for dedicated-managed audit storage — finance view required.
- Ensure templates do not leak any sample PII.
- Demo: ask Samir if we can have a short demo showing audit logs flowing to Splunk during the pilot.

Follow-ups before finalizing slides
- Get legal blueline by 2026-03-12.
- Confirm pilot customers (2) and schedule demo by 2026-03-20.
- Draft blog outline and run by comms (Ruth) by 2026-03-18.

Additional snippets (boilerplate Qs) to drop into Q&A doc
- "How do we prove retention settings were honored?" -> Provide audit log sample + how-to for generating retention proof with CLI.
- "If a customer requests deletion, what is the flow?" -> Documented steps: request -> ticket -> confirm retention offset -> run deletion job -> publish deletion report.

Final tone reminders
- Keep it concrete and non-legal-sounding in the all-hands. Use "we will publish" and "we will ship" language rather than "we may consider".
- Avoid promising timeline hard dates in public comms; internal timeline ok for planning.

Draft closing line
- "We want Redwood to be the easiest place to run inference when you need both control and performance. This is one step toward making that promise verifiable — for you and for our customers."

Unresolved items (TBD list)
- exact config key names
- storage cost guidance for managed deployments
- definitive field list for audit logs (legal sign-off)
